rules.rule: Photographing government buildings, military installations, checkpoints, and presidential palaces is strictly prohibited. This includes certain airports and ports. Authorities are highly sensitive to unauthorized filming of security personnel. Security guards may ask you to delete photos immediately; refusal can lead to arrest.
rules.penalty: Confiscation of equipment, heavy fines starting from 10,000 AED, and possible detention/deportation. Legal basis: UAE Federal Law No. 3 of 1987 (Penal Code).

location.name: Qasr Al Watan / Presidential Palace Area

rules.rule: Every tourist or resident MUST carry their original passport (for tourists) or Emirates ID (for residents) at all times. Police have the legal right to stop any individual for a random document check. Photocopies are often rejected during street checks. If you do not have your ID, you can be detained until verified.
rules.penalty: Detention at a police station until identity is confirmed. Possible deportation if visa is expired. Legal basis: Federal Decree-Law No. 29 of 2021.

rules.rule: Sharjah is a 'dry' emirate. Possessing or consuming alcohol is strictly forbidden. Even carrying sealed alcohol in your vehicle while passing through Sharjah can lead to arrest if stopped by police. Do not bring alcohol from Dubai into Sharjah.
rules.penalty: Fine up to 5,000 AED and up to 6 months in prison + mandatory deportation for non-nationals. Legal basis: Sharjah Alcohol Prohibition Law.

rules.rule: During Ramadan, eating, drinking (even water), or smoking in public during daylight hours is a criminal offense. While Dubai has relaxed mall restaurant rules (allowing screening), it remains illegal to consume food on the street or in public parks. This applies to non-Muslims as a mark of respect.
rules.penalty: Fine of up to 2,000 AED or up to 1 month imprisonment. Legal basis: Article 313 of UAE Penal Code.

rules.rule: The UAE maintains world-class anti-narcotics enforcement. Under 2024 reforms, first-time travelers found with 'trace' amounts for personal use may face a mandatory fine (AED 5k-20k) and confiscation at the airport instead of prison. However, any amount intended for others is treated as trafficking and carries extreme penalties.
rules.penalty: Confiscation + deportation for tourists. Life imprisonment/death penalty for trafficking. Legal basis: Federal Law No. 14 of 1995 (updated 2024).

rules.rule: Public displays of affection (PDA) — including kissing or suggestive behavior — are considered an 'outrage on public decency.' Holding hands for married couples is generally fine, but excessive intimacy in public can lead to arrest if reported by residents.
rules.penalty: Fine of 5,000 AED and possible imprisonment + deportation. Legal basis: Article 358 of UAE Penal Code.

rules.rule: Photographing identifiable individuals (especially women and children) without their explicit consent is a major criminal offense. Posting such 'street photos' on social media can lead to immediate prosecution if the subject reports it. Privacy is a constitutional right in the UAE.
rules.penalty: Fine between 150,000 AED and 500,000 AED and 6 months in prison + deportation. Legal basis: Article 44 of UAE Cybercrime Law.

rules.rule: The UAE uses a 'Black Point' system. Accumulating 24 points leads to license suspension. For tourists, fines are charged to the rental agency. Excessive speeding (80km/h+ over) results in immediate vehicle impoundment. Using a phone while driving is monitored by AI cameras.
rules.penalty: Fines from 400 to 3,000 AED. Impoundment for 60 days for racing. Using phone: 800 AED + 4 Black points. Legal basis: Ministerial Resolution No. 178.

rules.rule: Sending 'offensive' or 'insulting' messages (including bad words) to someone on WhatsApp or social media is a crime. If reported, digital logs are evidence for prosecution. This includes disparaging the UAE government or leadership.
rules.penalty: Fine up to 500,000 AED and deportation. Legal basis: Federal Decree-Law No. 34 of 2021.

rules.rule: Modest dress is expected in public. Malls require shoulders and knees covered. Swimwear is for beaches/pools ONLY; walking to a shop in a bikini is an offense. Cross-dressing is strictly illegal and leads to arrest.
rules.penalty: Police warning followed by fine/removal. Cross-dressing: Mandatory imprisonment + deportation. Legal basis: Dubai Code of Conduct.

rules.rule: Gambling is strictly illegal (including online). As of 2024, the GCGRA was created for future regulation, but currently, all betting remains a criminal offense. Participating in a private poker game for money is also prosecutable.
rules.penalty: Fine up to 20,000 AED or 2 years imprisonment. Legal basis: Article 414 of UAE Penal Code.

rules.rule: Littering in the desert or on public beaches is heavily fined. This includes leaving BBQ charcoal or cigarette butts. Beach Marshals and cameras monitor popular spots like JBR and Kite Beach.
rules.penalty: Fine of 500 AED for first offense. Waste near BBQ: 1,000 AED. Legal basis: Federal Law No. 24.

rules.rule: Raising funds or solicitating donations (even for charity) without a prior permit from IACAD is illegal. Don't post GoFundMe links from a UAE IP address; it triggers cyber-financial filters.
rules.penalty: Fine of 200,000 AED to 500,000 AED and imprisonment. Legal basis: Federal Law No. 3.

rules.rule: Dubai Metro etiquette: (1) No eating/drinking/gum. (2) No sleeping/napping at stations. (3) Men must NEVER enter the 'Women & Children' pink zone; even by accident, fine is immediate.
rules.penalty: Eating: 100 AED. Sleeping: 300 AED. Wrong Cabin: 100 AED. Legal basis: RTA Metro Regulations.

rules.rule: Flying recreational drones is currently BANNED in most UAE residential/commercial areas following security protocols. Permits are for commercial/media use only via GCAA. Using a drone near an airport is a major federal offense.
rules.penalty: Fines from 50,000 AED + prison. Legal basis: GCAA Civil Aviation Regulations.

rules.rule: Dubai's 'Salik' is a gate-based toll system. If you pass a gate with no tag or low balance, you have 5 days to top up, or a fine is issued. Rental agencies charge this automatically + their own fee.
rules.penalty: Fine up to 400 AED per violation. Legal basis: RTA Dubai Salik Policy.

rules.rule: Jaywalking is strictly fined in 2024/2025. Crossing on a red pedestrian light or outside a zebra crossing is a violation. Police conduct frequent 'Stop Jaywalking' campaigns in Deira and Bur Dubai.
rules.penalty: Fine of 400 AED via on-the-spot ticket or CCTV. Legal basis: Federal Traffic Law.

rules.rule: Profanity, swearing, or offensive hand gestures (middle finger) toward others are criminal acts. Even 'road rage' swearing can lead to a police report and jail time for tourists.
rules.penalty: Fine up to 10,000 AED and deportation. Legal basis: Article 373 of UAE Penal Code.

rules.rule: Taking photos or videos of road accidents or victims is strictly forbidden. This also includes 'rubbernecking' to gawk at scenes. This is to protect victim privacy and prevent traffic flow disruption.
rules.penalty: Fine of 1,000 AED + points + potential arrest under cybercrime law. Legal basis: UAE Ministry of Interior Decree.

rules.rule: Controlled medications (antidepressants, painkillers with codeine) require prior MoHAP online approval. Without a valid attested prescription and permit, it is treated as drug entry violation.
rules.penalty: Confiscation + arrest + prison. Legal basis: MoHAP Controlled List.
